question: Does the per-slab whole-history KV import in _sync_packed_decode_initial_state cause the multi-chunk packed slot-local prefill slowdown, and is removing it safe?
answer: Removal is safe and exact (zero KV-import calls on the eligible route, identical final-logit sha256 and 8-token greedy sequences at 1/2/4/8 chunks, Conv/GDN imports unchanged), but it is NOT the long-prompt bottleneck: prefill wall time is unchanged at every measured shape (121.770 -> 121.862 s at 8 chunks). The import was 910 MiB / 7,168 memcpy dispatches of dead work at 8 chunks; the earlier attribution of the slowdown to this import is disproven at these shapes and withdrawn. The real bottleneck remains open; kernel-family attribution with prewarmed, cached-build profiling is the queued follow-up.
change: _sync_packed_decode_initial_state gains copy_kv=True (mirroring _scatter_packed_decode_state's copy_kv); the FULL_ATTENTION branch skips the whole-history KV segment copies when copy_kv=False while the Conv/GDN linear-state import is preserved. _prefill_batch_native_single_slab passes copy_kv=not slot_local_full_prefill after final route resolution (after the device_kv_nonidentity_scatter / direct_int8 adjustments). Non-slot-local fallback paths and the packed decode rounds keep the default import.

protocol.harness: scripts/gguf_packed_kv_import_profile.py --rows 1024,2048,4096,8192 (new; counts _copy_session_packed_kv_segments calls/rows/memcpy dispatches/bytes via runtime.memcpy_async wrapping, _sync call count, fused linear-state copies; wall time of the synchronized prefill; a second pass with stream/device synchronization neutralized for CPU submission; final-logits sha256 + 8 greedy decode IDs)
protocol.prompt: deterministic varied prompt, numpy default_rng(20260910), token IDs in [1000, 32000)
protocol.kv: int8_per_token_head, FP32 per-token/head scales, max_sequence_length 16384 (route int8_direct, no mirror, slot-local full attention)
protocol.control: pre-fix run on the committed tree (16c9c716f / ca21f09fa) in the same session, before the runner change; post-fix run on the working tree afterwards
caveats: CPU submission ~= wall does NOT establish device-bound execution: the neutralized-synchronization pass can still block on a full command queue (GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=1), so it is an upper bound on host enqueue time, not a host-bound proof
per-chunk cost growth is not established linear: 4 -> 8 chunks takes wall 18.015 -> 121.862 s (6.8x for 2x the chunks)

no kernel-family GPU-time attribution is included; two rocprofv3 attempts stalled in hipcc --version compiler-version discovery under the profiler and were stopped; the follow-up profile must prewarm the JIT cache, pass HIPENGINE_COMPILER_VERSION_FILE and HIPENGINE_REQUIRE_CACHED_BUILD=1

tests: tests/test_gguf_packed_kv_import_skip.py: 4 host-policy tests (copy_kv=False skips KV segments and keeps the linear import; default keeps the whole-history import; copy_linear_state=False skips only the linear side; position-zero slab imports nothing either way). Prefill/packed/INT8-KV bundle + new files: 165 passed, 5 skipped.
not_a_perf_claim: Wall time is unchanged at every measured shape. This change removes dead copy work (dispatches, bytes, host segment walking) and the quadratic import's memory traffic; it is not a throughput improvement and no topline row moves.
